findings: Déf. 1′ (benzecri1960_ch3.tex:889–892) is imprecise. With closed half-lines (the reading forced by « en un point distinct des extrémités a et a′ », l.890–891), W_a is the union iff W ⊄ {a, a′} (coneAppui_eq_demiDroitesFermeesW_iff): it fails only in the degenerate cases W = {a} and W = {a, a′} (both in K(S(E)); e.g. always when dim E = 1). For W = {a}, Déf. 1 gives W_a = {a, a′} (coneAppui_singleton) while the union is empty (demiDroitesFermeesW_singleton); degenerate-case refutation not_def1prime_closed, every nonzero E.

Corrected form, valid with no exception (W convex, a ∈ W): W_a = {a, a′} ∪ ⋃ open half-lines (coneAppui_eq_insert_demiDroitesW; coneAppui_diff_eq_demiDroitesW). With the library's open halfLine convention the union alone never contains a′ (coneAppui_ne_demiDroitesW), a fact about that convention, not an error of the paper.
questions: « demi-droite » in Déf. 1′: Chapter 1 does not say whether a half-line contains its ends. Reading taken: closed (ends included), as « distinct des extrémités » implies; under it Déf. 1′ holds iff W ⊄ {a, a′}. The open reading is formalized too.

Convex parts of S(E) are stable under ⋂₀ in one line through isConvexPart_iff_isSegConvex (isConvexPart_sInter); a closed segment, antipodal ends included, is a convex part (isConvexPart_closedSeg); the closure of a convex part is one (IsConvexPart.closure, via F_closure and closure_singleton).
Inside `theorem IsConvexPart.closure`, the bare name `closure` resolves to the theorem itself in the proof: write `_root_.closure`.
